page: Amazon Web Services r5a.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7571 processor. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and utilizes the x86_64 architecture. Local storage is not included, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the r5a.2xlarge exhibits modest compute and memory performance. In stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, the instance scores in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests for large blocks (256MB uncached) also fall into the bottom 10%, with read speeds at 21.56 GB/sec and write speeds at 11.76 GB/sec. However, the Passmark CPU score and CPU encryption tests achieve average performance, placing in the middle 50%. Text generation for small language models also performs at an average level, though larger model inference and general database operations show weaker results.

The primary tradeoff of the r5a.2xlarge is its lower compute and memory throughput relative to its large memory capacity. While it offers a substantial 64.0 GB RAM allocation, the underlying AMD EPYC 7571 hardware limits its performance in CPU-intensive tasks. This profile makes the instance qualitatively cost-effective for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-speed processing or high sequential memory bandwidth. Suitable workloads include caching layers, moderate database operations, and memory-intensive applications with lower CPU demands.
